title: Keep USAGM security clearance duties with DOD and OPM
proposal: The text recommends that the U.S. Agency for Global Media (USAGM) not regain control over its own personnel security and suitability checks, which should stay with the Defense Department and OPM.
quote: These responsibilities must remain with the Department of Defense and the Office of Personnel Management

title: Cut USAGM's budget to under $700 million a year
proposal: The text states that USAGM can operate on less than $700 million per year, compared with the more than $800 million it says was spent before mid-2020.
quote: can be conducted on less than $700 million per year. Prior to the arrival of President Donald Trump’s appointees

title: Consolidate duplicate language services across USAGM networks
proposal: The text recommends combining redundant services, such as Mandarin and Farsi programs offered by both Voice of America and other USAGM-funded networks.
quote: Fiscal responsibility and transparency should return to the USAGM, with consolidation being a cornerstone of the strategy.

title: Replace the Open Technology Fund with USAGM's Office of Internet Freedom
proposal: The text recommends fully bringing back USAGM's in-house Office of Internet Freedom, whose role and funding it says the Open Technology Fund took over, so the agency and Congress can oversee that spending.
quote: within this agency. Full reinstatement of OIF would allow full agency and

title: Stop using J-1 exchange visas to hire foreign journalists
proposal: The text says USAGM should use the I visa meant for foreign journalists rather than J-1 cultural exchange visas, which it says are used to fill jobs Americans could do.
quote: the USAGM uses the J-1 “cultural exchange” visas to allow foreign nationals to transition easily into jobs that American citizens

title: Invest in shortwave radio broadcasting
proposal: The text recommends renewed budget support for USAGM's shortwave radio stations, which it says are vital if undersea internet cables are damaged in a major conflict.
quote: Non-web-based technologies that are proven and durable, such as shortwave radio transmission stations, have been grossly deemphasized in budgeting

title: End nepotism and improper hiring at USAGM
proposal: The text recommends enforcing federal hiring laws and national security vetting at USAGM and its grantees, and making policy changes to end nepotism and improper hiring.
quote: Government hiring policies and federal law must be followed, and serious policy changes must be implemented to end these practices.

title: Put Voice of America under NSC or State Department control
proposal: The text recommends placing VOA in the direct chain of command under the National Security Council or, if not, under the State Department's Office of Global Public Affairs. It also suggests the whole agency could come under the NSC, State, or both.
quote: serious consideration should be given to putting VOA under the direct supervision of the Office of Global Public Affairs at the Department of State

title: Coordinate VOA messaging with State Department social media
proposal: The text recommends that taxpayer-funded broadcasting that tells America's story be coordinated with the State Department's foreign-language social media platforms.
quote: Ensuring that taxpayer-funded TV , radio, and messaging tells America’s story is imperative and should be coordinated with the existing

title: Give the Secretary of State a real say on the USAGM board
proposal: The text recommends that the Secretary of State's seat on the agency's board become meaningful and directive, and that senior State public affairs officials be accountable for agency actions.
quote: This position should be relevant and directive when U.S. foreign policy and strategic communications are at stake.

title: Install acting USAGM leadership while a CEO awaits confirmation
proposal: The text recommends putting effective leaders in place, even in acting roles, while a new USAGM chief executive waits for Senate confirmation.
quote: Employing effective leadership, even in an acting capacity, while a new CEO is awaiting Senate confirmation is necessary

title: Overhaul USAGM with Congress to streamline and cut waste
proposal: The text recommends a top-to-bottom overhaul of USAGM, done with congressional review and support, to modernize, streamline and reduce waste.
quote: An overhaul of the agency with review from Congress to modernize, streamline, and reduce waste must be done with congressional support.

title: Defund and shut down USAGM if it cannot be reformed
proposal: The text says that if the agency keeps repeating what it calls adversaries' propaganda, USAGM should lose its funding and be abolished.
quote: In that case, the USAGM should be defunded and disestablished.

title: End federal funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting
proposal: The text recommends ending taxpayer funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, which funds NPR and PBS, including by the President refusing to sign any spending bill that funds it.
quote: the next conservative President must finally get this done and do it despite opposition from congressional members of his own party if necessary

title: End advance appropriations for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting
proposal: The text recommends ending the special practice of funding the CPB two years ahead of time.
quote: This special budgetary treatment is unjustified and should be ended.

title: Strip NPR and PBS stations of noncommercial educational status
proposal: The text recommends that the President direct the FCC to remove PBS- and NPR-affiliated stations from the noncommercial educational (NCE) category, ending benefits like reserved frequencies and fee exemptions.
quote: The next President should instruct the FCC to exclude the stations affiliated with PBS and NPR from the NCE denomination and the privileges that come with it.
